comparison: Perfect agreement on MIES establishment (C1, C12-C18). Both evaluations find the behavioral observations, sensory modality testing, and genetic experiments fully supported. OpenEval emphasizes the ~30 min EHP reduction and Orco mutant data; peer reviewers explicitly affirm these foundational observations with no concerns raised.

Perfect agreement on Or47b role (C2, C19-C26). Both evaluations find the loss-of-function, gain-of-function, and rescue experiments compelling. OpenEval highlights genetic specificity through heterozygous controls; peer reviewers describe experiments as 'thorough and systematic' and 'rigorous' with no methodological concerns.

Perfect agreement on 2MC identification and specificity (C4, C27-C40). Both evaluations support the dose-response experiments, genetic specificity tests, and species distribution correlations. OpenEval emphasizes negative results with other ligands strengthen specificity; peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the 2MC specificity findings without concerns.

Strong agreement on 7-T/ppk23 pathway (C3, C5, C41-C52). Both evaluations support the behavioral experiments, pheromone specificity, and neuronal silencing data. OpenEval addresses 11 of 14 peer-reviewed claims, noting functional redundancy in channel genes; peer reviewers affirm the ppk23 neuron experiments and 7-T identification without concerns.

Perfect agreement on cAMP signaling mechanism (C6, C66-C72). Both evaluations find the CRE-luciferase assays, subtype specificity, and dose-response correlations well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes mating-status dependence consistent with connectome data; peer reviewers explicitly note the pC1b,c subtype specificity without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on pC1 neuron roles (C7-C8, C53-C63). Both evaluations support the optogenetic silencing experiments and differential subtype functions. OpenEval addresses 13 claims including detailed subtype analysis; peer reviewers address 11 claims, explicitly noting acceptance of subtype-specific manipulations in the revision and finding 'convincing evidence' for pC1b,c integration role.

Strong agreement on cAMP sufficiency via PhotoAC (C9-C11, C73-C74, C78-C81). Both evaluations support the optogenetic adenylyl cyclase experiments showing EHP reduction, enhanced excitability, and increased remating. OpenEval addresses 12 claims; peer reviewers address 9 claims, describing the PhotoAC demonstration of increased cAMP effects without concerns.

Partial overlap on Dh44R dispensability (C76-C77). OpenEval includes this as part of broader PhotoAC/cAMP sufficiency analysis, interpreting it as suggesting alternative GPCR involvement. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this negative result without raising concerns, treating it as a valid mechanistic constraint.

Minimal overlap on pC1 background literature (C53-C55). OpenEval includes these as part of comprehensive pC1 neuron role analysis. Peer reviewers address these as established background facts about the receptivity circuit without questioning them.

Moderate agreement on pC1 courtship integration background (C64-C65, C110-C114). Both evaluations support these literature-based claims. OpenEval emphasizes connectome data (C127-C128) and mating-status-dependent cAMP differences (C126); peer reviewers affirm the broader context of pC1 neurons in the receptivity circuit without challenging the background.

Minimal overlap on connectome interpretation (C126-C128). OpenEval includes these as part of courtship cue integration analysis with SUPPORTED evaluation. Peer reviewers group these with broader background/discussion claims, implicitly accepting them without specific comment.

Strong agreement on background literature (C82-C109, C115-C118). Both evaluations support these literature-based claims establishing conceptual framework. OpenEval addresses 32 background claims as appropriately cited; peer reviewers address 40 claims including these, affirming the broader context without challenging the background information.

Agreement on speculative/discussion claims (C119-C125, C129-C131) but different evaluation types. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative interpretations requiring validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, treating discussion points as acceptable speculation. Both acknowledge these are not primary experimental findings but differ in how strictly they evaluate speculative content.

Minimal overlap on future work speculation (C129). OpenEval includes this as part of speculative claims rated UNCERTAIN. Peer reviewers implicitly accept it without specific comment, suggesting it falls within acceptable discussion speculation.
